title: Hublet + Rail proposal — decision log and grooming notes
body:
Purpose:
Short working record for the new "hublet" + rail navigation proposal. Captures rationale, wireframe observations from the 2024-11 sketch session, grooming decisions, open questions, and mapping to backlog tickets. Intended audience: product, design, eng (console front-end + routing), solutions engineers helping with demos.

Summary (one-liner):
Introduce small, context-sensitive "hublets"—compact micro-hubs that sit above a condensed rail—to reduce global sidebar bloat, improve discoverability for task flows, and enable fast deep-links for model-specific workflows.

Why this? Problem statement:
- Console top-level list is growing: models, routes, deployments, rollouts, audits, evals, optimize, observe, infra, org settings. New features keep getting added to the main rail and users report cognitive overload.
- Current left-heavy layout pushes task context to subpages; users must navigate 3+ clicks to reach common cross-cutting flows (e.g., model compare + rollout + cost analysis).
- We need better surface area for ephemeral task flows (A/B experiments, canaries, on-call debug tools) without permanently adding top-level nav items.

Key proposal (concept):
- Primary rail: global targets (Home, Workspaces, Models, Deployments, Billing, Admin). Keep it stable and minimal.
- Hublet: a compact, transient horizontal element that appears below header when a high-level rail item is active (or pinned). Hublets surface the most relevant task clusters for that context.
  - Example: when on Models, hublet shows: Catalog, Pin/Version, Eval sets, Compare, Quantization profiles.
  - When on Deployments, hublet shows: Instances, Autoscale, Rollouts, Logs, Fallbacks.
- Raillet behavior: hublet can be collapsed, pinned per-user, and stored in workspace preferences.
- Deep-linking: every hublet item maps to a stable URL and telemetry tag so experiments and support links can point straight into a hublet flow.

Wireframe notes from sketch session (observations):
- Sketch A: Hublet as row of compact cards with 40–48px icons + two-line labels. Tested with 6 items -> comfortable on 1280px width.
- Sketch B: Hublet as segmented control (text-heavy) — better for accessibility but consumes vertical space.
- Decision: start with compact card row and add a11y variant toggle (larger labels) in user prefs.
- Transition animation: slide-down for appearance, fade-in for individual hublet cards. Avoid janky layout shifts—render a small placeholder height during load.

Routing semantics (engineering constraints):
- Rule 1: Global rail routes remain canonical (e.g., /models, /deployments). Hublet items are subroutes under canonical path (e.g., /models/compare, /deployments/rollouts).
- Rule 2: Hublet visibility determined by route metadata (server-provided or manifest). This keeps SPA routing logic simple and allows backend to suggest experiment-specific hublets.
- Rule 3: Breadcrumbs: primary rail item + hublet label + page title. Example: Models > Compare > model-123.
- Rule 4: Model pinning overlays should not change route identity (use query param ?pin=model-123) so that shareable links are preserved.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Hublet renders for Models and Deployments (two contexts) behind a feature flag.
- Each hublet item navigates to an existing or new page with stable URL and telemetry.
- Pin and collapse state persists per-user.
- No change to existing global rail order for non-feature-flag users.
- Accessibility: hublet keyboard nav and screen reader labels implemented.

Backlog mapping (rough grooming):
- CONS-1423: Hublet component and visual spec (design).
- CONS-1424: Hublet manifest API (platform) — expose context->hublet list.
- CONS-1425: Hublet client integration + routing metadata.
- CONS-1426: User prefs (pin/collapse storage).
- CONS-1427: Deep-link telemetry + canonical URL handling.
- CONS-1428: Acceptance testing + axe accessibility tests.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should hublet be purely client-only (derived from route) or server-driven (allows product experiments without code deploy)? We prefer server-driven manifest for experiments but need fallback for offline/local dev.
- How many hublet items is too many? Heuristic: limit to 6. If >6, surface 4 + "more" menu that opens the full sidebar for the context.
- Mobile: collapse into a single pulldown under header. Need separate high-fidelity mobile wireframes.
- Analytics: need clear mapping of hublet impressions, clicks, and time-to-first-action. Instrumentation requirement in CONS-1427.

Risk log:
- Hidden discoverability: users may not notice hublets if collapsed by default. Mitigation: initial tour step and inline hints for first N users.
- Performance: adding hublet manifest calls on route change could add latency. Mitigation: cache manifest per-workspace and prefetch for frequently used rails.

Design notes / micro-interactions:
- Hover states show short helper tooltip + keyboard shortcut.
- Right-side contextual overflow shows quick actions (e.g., "Create eval set") so users can start flows without a full page load.
- When a hublet item represents an ongoing workflow (e.g., canary running), show a subtle progress indicator and the ability to open slim modal to quick-check status.

Accessibility checklist (quick):
- All hublet items must be reachable via tab.
- Icon-only hublets require aria-labels.
- Contrast and focus rings per design system.

Experimental rollout plan:
1) Internal dogfood (console@redwood): enable feature flag for 20% of engineering org. Collect qualitative feedback via forms and Slack.
2) Canary to 5% of external users with high-engagement workspaces. Measure time-to-task and support tickets.
3) Gradual ramp to all users with opt-out setting.

Decision log (current):
- Start with compact hublet row (NOT segmented control). — APPROVED 2024-11-19 (product + design).
- Implement manifest API (server-driven) with client fallback to static mapping. — APPROVED 2024-12-03 (platform + eng).
- Limit to 6 visible items + "more" menu. — APPROVED 2024-12-17 (product).

Next steps (short):
- Design: produce high-fidelity desktop + mobile hublet variants (Samira) — due 2024-11-22.
- Backend: spec manifest API and feature-flag gating (Luis) — draft by 2024-11-30.
- Frontend: implement basic hublet layout + routing metadata reading (Ethan) — spike in sprint 12.
- UX research: plan 6 unmoderated tasks to validate discoverability and speed gains — Maya to own.

Notes to self / rough TODOs (informal):
- add a short explainer to onboarding checklist for new users ("Quick tour: hublets").
- correlate hublet clicks with eval regressions (are users using hublet->eval more?).
- check overlap with "quick actions" currently in header — avoid duplication.

Misc (links and sketches):
- Sketch folder: drive:/product/console-and-rollouts/sketches/hublet-2024-11-12.png
- Quick prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/hublet-proto (private)

If you want to riff on labels or suggest different heuristics for limiting items, add comments below. This doc will be incrementally updated as spike results come in.

-- Priya
